newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec real earnings rose 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec real earnings rose 1.1 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 1.1 percent in December, the Labor Department said Tuesday.
The December increase followed a 1.0 percent rise in November real average weekly earnings.

The December rise stems from a 0.9 percent rise in average weekly hours, a 0.5 percent increase in average hourly earnings and a 0.3 percent rise in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers.
Real average weekly earnings in December were up 1.8 percent from December last year, the department said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $259.98 in December, versus $257.09 in November and $255.11 in December 1995.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $419.34 in December, compared with $413.66 in November and $398.22 in December last year.
